description: Bacterial soft rot is a destructive disease of cabbage that causes rapid decay of plant tissues. The bacteria enter through wounds or natural openings and spread quickly in warm and humid conditions. The disease can occur in the field but often causes serious losses during storage and transportation.
symptoms: Water-soaked spots on leaves or cabbage heads
Soft, sunken lesions that enlarge rapidly
Tissues become soft, mushy, and wet
Discoloration from cream to brown or black
Leaves, stems or roots may completely decay in severe infections
visual_signature: wet soft rot on cabbage tissue
dark rotting areas with liquid leakage
favorable_conditions: plant wounds caused by insects or tools
management: Use healthy and disease-free planting material
Handle plants carefully to avoid wounds
Remove and destroy infected plants immediately
Rotate crops with non-host plants for at least 3 years
Ensure proper plant nutrition especially calcium
prevention: Keep storage areas clean and dry
storage_management: Avoid storing damaged or infected vegetables
Use soft materials like straw or paper to prevent injuries
